title: From Flatland to Forest: Exploring Pareto-optimal Design through RTL Hierarchy Trees
problem: Design space exploration (DSE) for modern hardware treats designs as flat parameter vectors, losing structural information. Current methods fail to exploit the hierarchical nature of RTL architectures, making exploration inefficient.
motivation: Growing hardware complexity demands better DSE methods that leverage inherent structural patterns in RTL hierarchies to navigate vast design spaces efficiently.
method: The approach creates a kernel—a mathematical comparison tool—that respects how hardware designs are structured: as nested hierarchies of components rather than flat lists of parameters. It weights this comparison by analyzing synthesis reports to determine which components matter most. A clustering algorithm then uses this weighted comparison to group designs with similar architectural patterns, enabling rapid exploration of many design options in parallel on Gemmini-based RISC-V processors.
key_novelty: This is the first application of structure-aware comparison tools to hardware design space exploration, enabling direct comparison of designs based on their hierarchical organization.
contributions: RTL hierarchy-aware kernel for direct comparison of hardware architectures
Weighted kernel extension incorporating module importance from synthesis reports
Clustering method for identifying and exploring distinct architectural patterns
Demonstrated efficiency gains on Gemmini RISC-V SoC design space
limitations: Evaluation limited to Gemmini-based RISC-V SoC; scalability to larger, more complex designs not discussed.
